message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most famous and influential composers who have made their mark in the United States:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Jazz‑inspired classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | Neoclassical, “American” sound | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Rodeo* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Broadway, symphonic | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film music | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | Modernist | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | Experimental, early modernism | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Minimalism, contemporary | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine*, *The Dharma at Big Sur* |
| **William Grant Still** (1895–1978) | African‑American composer, “American Classical” | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird*, *The Spirit of the Black Hills* |
| **Ethel Smyth** (not American but influential in the US) | — | — |

These composers span a wide range of styles—from jazz-infused classics to minimalist film scores—and have helped shape the identity of American music on both the concert stage and in popular culture.
